newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania vows tough action on ex-communist blast.
newsitem.headline: Albania vows tough action on ex-communist blast.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Wednesday blamed former communist secret police for a blast that wrecked the apartment of a senior appeals court judge, injuring him and his daughter, and promised a tough response.
"This was an act of the former Albanian secret police...which committed monstrous crimes against the Albanian people (in the past)," Berisha told Radio Tirana.
"I guarantee the...determination of the Albanian state to face crime forcefully and give terrorists what they deserve," he added.

No-one was killed in the explosion but judge Prel Martini, 40, his six-year-old daughter Dea and neighbour Kozeta Prendi, 34, were injured, state radio said. Dea's condition was stable while her parents were in shock.
The attack almost completely destroyed Martini's Tirana apartment and damaged the fifth and sixth floors of the building.
Prime Minister Alexander Meksi was also quick to pin the blast on ex-communists.

"I think the authors of the explosion had political motives. It is...those forces of the secret police Sigurimi of the ex-communist regime that aim to destabilise Albanian democracy," he told reporters.
Judge Martini traced the motive to an appeals court decision on Tuesday that upheld prison sentences meted out to nine senior former communist officials. The nine will serve up to 20 years in jail.
Police said they did not know what kind of device caused the explosion. A special group has been set up to investigate.
Security was stepped up on Wednesday in the capital, with a heavier than usual police presence causing traffic congestion.
Four people were killed and 27 injured last February when a car bomb exploded in central Tirana.
Police later arrested members of what they called a guerrilla organisation comprising former communist secret police and charged them with planting the bomb.
